security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, inline file paths, or documentation snippets, so they are false positives. I confirmed the git pull and Gradle execution instructions because they can modify the workspace or execute project code. I found no prompt injection, credential collection, data exfiltration, or obfuscated payload in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote update command in normal workflow
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running git pull origin main, and state that it can change the working tree.

remediation.issue: Gradle build and server commands execute project code
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before running Gradle commands in untrusted repositories, and prefer sandboxed environments for verification.
Separate command examples from file-path references and label executable commands as steps requiring user approval.

content.value_statement: Backend changes can drift from project conventions, database docs, and test expectations. This skill gives a structured Spring Boot/MyBatis workflow from task intake through API, data, tests, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Plans REST controller, service, mapper, entity, and DTO work for Spring Boot projects.
Uses existing product.util helpers, logging aspects, and exception handlers before adding new logic.
Defines Flyway migration and database documentation steps for schema changes.
Requires JUnit, Mockito, MyBatis tests, lint checks, and coverage targets.
Prompts OpenAPI, error code, and completion report updates.
limitations: Assumes a Java backend using Spring Boot, MyBatis, Flyway, Gradle, and the documented project layout.
Does not implement frontend, mobile, infrastructure, or deployment workflows.
Local verification depends on available project tools, databases, and test fixtures.
Commands should be reviewed before execution in untrusted repositories.

use_cases.title: Add a new REST endpoint
use_cases.description: Follow the project sequence for DTOs, controllers, services, mappers, tests, and OpenAPI updates.

use_cases.title: Change a database model
use_cases.description: Plan Flyway migrations, mapper changes, database documentation, and regression tests in one workflow.

use_cases.title: Review implementation readiness
use_cases.description: Check branch state, issue linkage, lint results, coverage, server startup, and final reporting before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Create a small endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a read-only API change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use develop-backend to implement a read-only Spring Boot endpoint for [feature]. Include DTOs, service logic, mapper changes, tests, and OpenAPI updates.

prompt_templates.title: Add schema-backed behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task with a new database table
prompt_templates.prompt: Use develop-backend for [feature] that needs a new table. Plan Flyway migration, entity, mapper XML, service rules, error codes, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor backend logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task that changes existing service code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use develop-backend to refactor [service area]. Preserve API behavior, reuse product.util helpers, remove duplicate logging, and verify lint, tests, and coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare release handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for final verification and reporting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use develop-backend to finish [issue number]. Validate server startup, endpoint behavior, migration application, documentation updates, and completion report contents.

output_examples.input: Add a user profile API with a new table.
output: A staged backend plan covering migration, DTOs, mapper, service, controller, OpenAPI, tests, and verification.
A completion checklist that includes branch checks, issue linkage, coverage, lint, server startup, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Refactor account service validation without changing API behavior.
output: A refactor approach that preserves controller contracts and moves business rules into the service layer.
A test plan for normal, boundary, and error cases with required Gradle verification.

output_examples.input: Prepare a backend task for handoff.
output_examples.output: A concise handoff summary covering changed layers, test results, documentation updates, and server startup confirmation.

best_practices: Confirm branch and issue context before changing backend files.
Search for existing utilities and patterns before adding new classes.
Run lint, tests, coverage, and server startup checks before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Do not duplicate request, response, SQL, or trace logging already handled by AOP.
Do not suppress warnings except for the documented Mockito generic exchange case.
Do not skip database, OpenAPI, or error-code documentation when behavior changes.

faq.question: What stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Spring Boot backends that use MyBatis, Flyway, Gradle, JUnit, Mockito, and project-specific documentation.

faq.question: Does it write frontend code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on backend API, service, database, mapper, validation, test, and documentation work.

faq.question: How does it avoid duplicate code?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to inspect existing utilities, logging aspects, and exception handlers before adding new implementation.

faq.question: What verification does it require?
faq.answer: It requires IDE warning review, Gradle checks, test success, coverage targets, and server startup verification.

faq.question: Can it update database documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Flyway migration planning and database design document updates when schema changes are needed.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Git and Gradle commands should be reviewed, especially when the repository or dependencies are untrusted.
